title: Improving First Nations water security through governance
authors: Alcantara, Longboat, Vanhooren

title: Public Utility Ownership in 19th-century America: The "Aberrant" Case of Water
authors: Masten, Scott E.

title: Fecal sludge management system approach for establishing policy framework in urban areas of Vientiane Capital, Lao PDR
authors: Sidlakone S.; Ichiki A.
exclusion_reason_detail: Examines fecal sludge collection/transport/treatment chain and regulatory capacity for managing it, not household-level legal/administrative access to a connection. All surveyed households already have on-site sanitation. Borderline -- flagged for second-reviewer attention; 8 other FSM papers in the pool may share this issue.

title: Leveraging Artificial Intelligence for Comprehensive Analysis of Community and Rural Aqueduct Systems
authors: Salazar-Gámez L. et al.
exclusion_reason_detail: AI-driven diagnostic study of 14 community aqueduct systems (Pasto, Colombia). Unit of analysis is the aqueduct system, not the household; outcomes are provider-side technical performance and the provider's own regulatory/tax compliance, not household legal/administrative access mechanisms. Core contribution is a GenAI diagnostic methodology.

title: Flows against the current: governance and politics of wastewater reuse in Valle Alto, Bolivia
authors: Saldías C.; Echeverría I.; Vargas V.; Saavedra O.
exclusion_reason_detail: Rich qualitative governance/institutional-bricolage study, but population/exposure is farmers accessing treated wastewater for agricultural irrigation, not household connection to a networked water/sanitation service. Borderline -- flagged for second-reviewer attention.

title: Financial insecurity among sanitation workers and its impacts on safe service reliability: a case study of the Arusha depot manual emptying group
authors: Kimwaga R.; Magambo H.; Ndezi T.
exclusion_reason_detail: Population/exposure is sanitation workers' financial insecurity affecting their own service delivery behavior, not households navigating legal/administrative access to a service. Labor-economics study of the supply side.

title: Co-Creating an Intersectional Water Justice Toolkit and Documentary in Cape Town, South Africa
authors: Puvaneyshwaran D. et al.
exclusion_reason_detail: Describes co-design of an advocacy toolkit and documentary film; reports no empirical outcome relevant to access, connection, service availability, reliability, quantity, affordability, or exclusion. A knowledge-mobilization/practice resource, not an empirical access study.

title: Assessing urban water security in Awash River Basin, Addis Ababa, and its surrounding towns using Integrated Urban Water Security Index
authors: Legass A.M. et al.
exclusion_reason_detail: Composite water-security index study dominated by hydrology, water-quality chemistry, GIS mapping, and climate modeling. Governance appears only as a single survey satisfaction item; no legal/administrative access mechanism is analyzed as an exposure variable.

title: Effectiveness of emergency WASH strategies in disaster-prone areas of Africa: a systematic review
authors: Chirwa E.; Mwalwanda A.; Soko M.; Mbakaya B.C.
exclusion_reason_detail: Systematic review of emergency WASH intervention effectiveness on health/disease outcomes (cholera) during disasters, not on access/connection/administrative outcomes. No legal or administrative access mechanism examined.

title: Responsible leadership and sustainability performance of health and sanitation projects: the mediating role of resilience
authors: Kyambade M.; Mwesigwa R.; Alinda K.; Tumwine S.; Lwanga F.
exclusion_reason_detail: PLS-SEM survey of project staff/implementers (n=520) across 86 health/sanitation projects in Uganda; exposure is leadership style, outcome is organizational sustainability performance -- not household legal/administrative access. Part of a related Kyambade et al. cluster on project-level sustainability/governance (see also RA8E99F31040E, R26FD0045CAAA, R5FB1EE86B250) that may share this issue -- not yet screened.

title: Water for All: A Strategic Assessment of Drinking Water Management at Cox's Bazar of Bangladesh in the Light of SDGs
authors: Molla M.H.; Chowdhury M.A.T.; Muhibbullah M.
exclusion_reason_detail: Stakeholder-perception SDG-alignment scorecard (Likert scores across 20 targets/6 SDGs) plus a technical supply-demand gap calculation. Community participation is one Likert item among 20; no specific legal/administrative access mechanism is traced against a household-level outcome.

title: Exploring the role of institutional governance in enhancing sustainability performance of health and sanitation projects in Uganda: a qualitative inquiry
authors: Kyambade M.; Mwesigwa R.; Alinda K.; Tumwine S.; Lwanga F.
exclusion_reason_detail: Qualitative institutional-theory inquiry (21 interviews with policymakers/health officers/project managers) into how governance shapes project-level 'sustainability performance', not household legal/administrative access. Same author cluster/scope issue as R4F8CFC42FFE1.

title: The Agency, Resources, and Institutional Structures for Sanitation-related Empowerment (ARISE) scales: Psychometric evaluation across eight cities in Asia and Africa
authors: Sinharoy S.S. et al.
exclusion_reason_detail: Psychometric scale-validation study (EFA/CFA, measurement invariance) of women's sanitation-related empowerment scales. Outcome is scale psychometric performance, not household access/connection/reliability/affordability. Related ARISE cluster papers in pool not yet screened.

title: Enablers and Obstacles in Integrated Water Resources Management (IWRM) Implementation and Their Contributions to Sustainable Territorial Development
authors: Gallegos A.; Grigg N.S.; Llano W.
exclusion_reason_detail: PRISMA systematic review of 375 IWRM implementation studies at basin/national/transboundary scale, linked to territorial development outcomes. No household-level access outcome examined anywhere.

title: Does Economic Growth Drive Equitable Water and Sanitation Access? Assessing Inequality Reduction Across 64 Nations
authors: García-López M.; López-Ruiz S.; Cuadrado-Quesada G.
exclusion_reason_detail: Cross-country econometric panel (64 nations, OLS/2SLS/SURE) testing GDP growth against aggregate JMP access-rate inequality; unit of analysis is the country, not the household. 'Governance effectiveness' is a generic macro index, not a specific legal/administrative access mechanism. Borderline -- flagged for second-reviewer attention.

title: Water Security in Fragile States: Mapping Governance and Water Access in Libya
authors: Ellinport B. et al.
exclusion_reason_detail: GIS-based composite water security index (natural availability + infrastructure investment) across Libya's 22 districts from secondary data only. Governance is thematic framing, not a specific access mechanism tied to measured household-level variation.

title: REVISITING: Off-grid, the New Water Supply Solution
authors: Gaudry A.; Colon M.; Baron C.
exclusion_reason_detail: Narrative/critical policy book chapter synthesizing secondary literature on off-grid water solutions; no primary empirical data or systematic review methodology of its own.

title: Drinking Water Quality Regulations: A Contrast Between Germany and Latin America
authors: Vogelmann E.S.; Prevedello J.; Tiruneh G.A.
exclusion_reason_detail: Comparative doctrinal/documentary analysis of drinking-water quality (chemical/microbiological) regulatory standards across countries. Unit of analysis is the legal text, outcome is regulatory stringency, not household access/connection.

title: Institutional trust as a critical determinant of households' willingness to pay for improved water services in Leku Town, Ethiopia
authors: Dumo W.M.
exclusion_reason_detail: Contingent valuation/WTP survey (n=193); institutional trust is an attitudinal/perceptual predictor, outcome is hypothetical willingness-to-pay, not an actual access/connection/reliability/affordability outcome.

title: Water, Sanitation and Health: The World Bank's Financing of Sustainable Development Goal 6
authors: Martínez-Gómez C.; Gallego-Valero L.; Moral-Pajares E.
exclusion_reason_detail: Country/project-level macro analysis of 546 World Bank financing projects using secondary aggregate data; unit of analysis is the country/project, not the household.

title: Knowledge, economic, and WASH challenges affecting menstrual health and hygiene among nursing students in Bangladesh using a mixed-methods approach
authors: Zaman M.N.U.; Sai A.; Yamauchi T.
exclusion_reason_detail: Mixed-methods study of menstrual health/hygiene among nursing students at educational institutions. Population is students, not households; WASH facility adequacy is a campus-level menstrual-management outcome, not household water/sanitation access.

title: Hydro-citizenship revisited: water, belonging, and the politics of adaptation in rough neighbourhoods in the Global South
authors: Bhanye J.
exclusion_reason_detail: Theoretical/conceptual 'Short Communication' re-theorizing hydro-citizenship via flood-adaptation politics; water/sanitation-specific access barriers are named citing another source, not the author's own data. Insufficient information to identify a water/sanitation population/exposure/outcome. Borderline; flagged for reviewer_2.

title: 'No Human Entry' on Paper: Outsourcing Labour, Implementation Gaps, and Everyday Illegality of Manual Scavenging in India
authors: Raj N.; Tiwari M.
exclusion_reason_detail: Secondary-source analysis of caste-based occupational exploitation of manual scavengers (sanitation workers) in India despite legal bans. Population is sanitation workers, outcome is labor exploitation/enforcement of anti-scavenging law, not household sanitation service access.

title: Optimal water tariffs and trade-offs: a multi-objective analysis of municipalities in Pernambuco
authors: De Lima e Silva A.; De Lima e Silva Y.C.; Alcoforado de Moraes M.M.G.
exclusion_reason_detail: Multi-objective optimization model generating a Pareto frontier of optimal water tariffs across 172 Brazilian municipalities. Unit of analysis is the municipality, outcome is a normative tariff-design solution set, not an observed household access/affordability outcome.

title: Resilience and Sustainability Performance of Health and Sanitation Projects in Uganda
authors: Kyambade M.; Mwesigwa R.; Alinda K.; Tumwine S.; Lwanga F.
exclusion_reason_detail: PLS-SEM survey (n=520 stakeholders: project staff, procurement/technical officers, regulatory officials, beneficiary reps) across 86 health/sanitation projects in Uganda; exposure is organizational resilience (shock absorption, adaptability, redundancy, learning/innovation), outcome is project-level sustainability performance (economic efficiency, social outcomes, environmental management) -- not household-level legal/administrative water/sanitation access. Third paper in the Kyambade et al. project-management cluster (see also R4F8CFC42FFE1, R26FD0045CAAA), same wrong-population/wrong-outcome issue.

title: Institutional conflicts of interest in regional water management: a case study of the water supply in the Taipei metropolitan area
authors: Chen C.-Y.; Cai Y.-S.; Hung Y.-J.; You G.J.-Y.
exclusion_reason_detail: Deterministic WEAP scenario-based hydro-economic simulation of the Taipei metropolitan multi-reservoir water supply system. Exposure/outcome are utility-level pricing, inter-basin transfer-payment mechanisms, and system-wide social loss/shortage under hydrological stress scenarios -- an engineering/economic optimization study, not an empirical household-level access study. Household affordability burden is raised only as a policy-implications discussion point in the conclusion, not measured as data or an outcome variable.

title: Governance, structure, and access: a Bayesian hierarchical analysis of water, sanitation, and hygiene in South Asia
authors: Azimi M.N.; Rahman M.M.
exclusion_reason_detail: Country-level panel analysis (Bayesian hierarchical linear model, 8 South Asian countries, 2000-2024, World Development Indicators data); unit of analysis is the country, not the household. Governance is a composite autoencoder-derived index built from six generic Worldwide Governance Indicators dimensions, not a specific legal/administrative access mechanism tied to household-level outcomes. Same cross-country composite-governance-index pattern as the earlier-excluded Garcia-Lopez (R5E653CCC67DF) and Gallegos (R2D6E5154CE63) papers.

title: A Systematic Overview of Institutional Pathways and Constraints in the Integration of Local and Indigenous Knowledge into Water Resource Policy: An African Perspective
authors: Ngubane Z.; Aliyu Yaro N.S.; Ziqubu S.M.; Adedeji J.A.
exclusion_reason_detail: Explicitly interpretive/conceptual thematic synthesis of 30 studies (authors state they do not follow formal PRISMA methodology); unit of analysis is institutional/governance systems across Africa generally, not households. No household-level water/sanitation access, connection, reliability, affordability, or administrative outcome is measured or synthesized anywhere. Same no-household-outcome pattern as the earlier-excluded Gallegos IWRM review (R2D6E5154CE63) and Garcia-Lopez cross-country panel (R5E653CCC67DF).

title: Examining awareness, implementation, and challenges of sustainable development goal 6 in rural Osun State, Nigeria
authors: Ogunbode T.O.; Awolola V.O.
exclusion_reason_detail: Household survey (n=310, 31 rural communities, Osun State, Nigeria) whose measured outcome, via factor analysis, is respondents' awareness of SDG 6 -- not a formal connection, effective/economic access, or administrative access outcome. Exposure factors identified (cultural beliefs, poverty, road connectivity, women's empowerment) drive awareness, not a legal/administrative access mechanism. MDG-era borehole functionality data is purely infrastructure-maintenance description, with no eligibility/application/discretion/enforcement process analyzed. Part of an Ogunbode SDG6-Nigeria cluster (see also R7050D3D0A9CF, R06AA2F649B92) not yet screened -- may share this issue.

title: Barriers to water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) cluster coordination during emergencies in sub-Saharan Africa: A scoping review
authors: Yimenu A.A.; Gemechu M.T.; Shimber E.T.; Ndugga P.
exclusion_reason_detail: JBI scoping review (39 studies) of barriers to inter-agency WASH humanitarian cluster coordination in sub-Saharan Africa emergencies. Unit of analysis is the coordination cluster/humanitarian agency, not the household; outcomes are funding continuity, local capacity, monitoring/accountability, and coordination effectiveness -- no household-level access outcome synthesized anywhere. Same emergency-WASH-effectiveness pattern as the earlier-excluded Chirwa review (R50C907E99BA5), one level further removed (agency coordination rather than health outcomes).

title: A Qualitative Exploration of Social Sustainability Performance in Health and Sanitation Projects
authors: Kyambade M.; Mwesigwa R.; Alinda K.; Tumwine S.; Lwanga F.
exclusion_reason_detail: Qualitative exploratory study (21 semi-structured interviews with community members, local council leaders, and project implementers) in central Uganda; outcome is 'social sustainability performance' of health/sanitation projects, not household-level legal/administrative water/sanitation access. Fourth and final paper in the Kyambade et al. project-management cluster (R4F8CFC42FFE1, R26FD0045CAAA, R5FB1EE86B250), same wrong-population/wrong-outcome issue.

title: Beyond access: WASH, public health, and sustainable development priorities in Africa—a narrative review
authors: Elmi A.H.; Ibrahim R.K.
exclusion_reason_detail: Explicitly a narrative review, not systematic -- authors state no formal quality appraisal or structured search strategy was undertaken. Continent-wide thematic synthesis of WASH inequalities and generic governance/infrastructure barriers, no specific legal/administrative mechanism analyzed, no household-level outcome data synthesized. Does not meet INCLUSION_EXCLUSION.md criterion 3's 'systematic empirical synthesis' standard; same pattern as Ngubane (R6E8BD60B13E0) and Gallegos (R2D6E5154CE63).

title: Drinking Water Supply Strategies for Archipelagic States: Scale-Constrained Systems and Off-Grid Solutions from Small Islands in Indonesia
authors: Plamonia N. et al.
exclusion_reason_detail: Comparative mixed-evidence engineering/economic feasibility study (secondary data, limited field verification) of off-grid water systems across 15 small Indonesian islands. Authors explicitly conclude (RQ-2) that 'service failure reflects structural scale incompatibility rather than institutional weakness', rejecting an institutional/administrative explanation for the access gap. No legal/administrative mechanism analyzed as exposure. Same engineering/technical-feasibility pattern as Legass, Ellinport, and Chen (Taipei WEAP).

title: A review of the drivers and barriers influencing the impact of Water, Sanitation and Hygiene on attendance and retention of pupils in primary schools in developing countries
authors: Adekunle E.; Ottoh F.; Osimen G.; Akinola A.
exclusion_reason_detail: Narrative review (Mini Review, not systematic) of drivers/barriers of WASH impact on school attendance and retention of pupils. Population is pupils/schools, not households; outcome is educational attendance/retention, not household-level water/sanitation access. No legal/administrative access mechanism analyzed. Same wrong-population pattern as Zaman (R762C6673156D) and Sinharoy ARISE (R8AC9D969EC05); same non-systematic narrative-review pattern as Elmi and Ibrahim (RF7BD856CF4EE).

title: The Economics of Household Water Access: A Review and Research Roadmap for "Water for All"
authors: Choumert-Nkolo J.; Phélinas P.
exclusion_reason_detail: Invited Annual Review narrative synthesis, explicitly distinguished by the authors from prior 'systematic reviews and meta-analyses' on water access, with no defined search strategy or inclusion criteria of its own. Contribution is a measurement-metrics critique and a methodological call to combine RCT and qualitative evaluation methods for water interventions -- a research-roadmap argument, not an empirical synthesis of legal/administrative access mechanisms. Governance/tenure/legal barriers appear only as brief citation-driven passing references, never analyzed as a specific mechanism tied to a measured household-level outcome.

title: NAVIGATING INDIA'S LEGAL GOVERNANCE IN WATER SECTOR: A SCRUTINY INTO NATIONAL PERFORMANCE UNDER SDG FRAMEWORK FOR CLEAN AND WASTEWATER MANAGEMENT IN INDIA
authors: Pegu K.; Samal K.P.
exclusion_reason_detail: Pure doctrinal legal commentary (INCLUSION_EXCLUSION.md exclusion criterion 1) analyzing India water governance legal architecture (JJM, AMRUT, Swachh Bharat Mission Urban) against SDG 6 targets, without empirical household-level access evidence. Sole primary empirical component is a groundwater-quality contamination case study of the Mancheswar industrial area (pH, hardness, TDS, heavy metals) -- water-quality science, not household legal/administrative access data.

title: The Effect of Climate Change on Menstrual Health: A Qualitative Study of Gabura Union, Shyamnagar, Satkhira, Bangladesh
authors: Yasmin F.
exclusion_reason_detail: Qualitative study (24 IDIs, 6 KIIs, 5 male short interviews) in coastal Bangladesh. Outcome is menstrual health (hygiene constraints, saline-water infections, stigma, menstrual irregularities from crop-loss malnutrition), not household-level water/sanitation access. Water scarcity/salinity examined as climate-health exposure, not a legal/administrative access mechanism. Same wrong-outcome pattern as Chirwa emergency-WASH review (R50C907E99BA5).

title: Assessing disaster vulnerability in an informal settlement of Cape Town, South Africa, through the MOVE framework
authors: Kunguma O.; Awah L.S.; Petersen I.; Lunga W.
exclusion_reason_detail: Mixed-methods disaster-vulnerability study (125-household survey) applying the MOVE framework (exposure/susceptibility/resilience to floods/fires) in a Khayelitsha informal settlement. Sanitation access is one susceptibility indicator among many, not the focal outcome; no legal/administrative access mechanism analyzed as exposure. Outcome is disaster vulnerability, not household water/sanitation access.

title: Profit shifting from Nigeria to Europe: The impact on human rights
authors: Etter-Phoya R.; Murray S.; Hall S.; Masiya M.; O’Hare B.
exclusion_reason_detail: Macroeconomic/econometric modeling study (GRADE model) estimating national-level impacts of corporate tax profit-shifting on Nigeria's aggregate rights fulfillment (water, sanitation, education, child survival). Core topic is international tax justice, not household-level legal/administrative water access; water access is one of several modeled downstream indicators extrapolated from national tax-revenue estimates, not observed household data. Part of an O'Hare/Etter-Phoya/Hall/Murray/Masiya tax-justice cluster (REF486158BFC4, R56488964E5E9, RE3B6CA880897) not yet screened.

title: The global sanitary revolution in historical perspective
authors: Gallardo-Albarrán D.
exclusion_reason_detail: Economic-history survey (no defined search strategy) of waterworks/sewerage diffusion ca. 1850-1950 in the Netherlands and Colombia, and its mortality impact. Core topic is historical infrastructure diffusion, not contemporary administrative law/legal-procedure access mechanisms. Author explicitly states the literature is insufficient to explain access differences, calling for future research rather than presenting a mature empirical finding. Borderline -- flagged for second-reviewer attention given partial overlap with the Netherlands comparator jurisdiction.

title: Urban Infrastructure Policy to Adapt to Technological and Social Change
authors: Grigg N.S.
exclusion_reason_detail: Conceptual/policy-analysis paper (systems approaches, IAD framework applied narratively) critiquing US infrastructure investment policy reports, drawing on secondary policy reports and EPA surveys, not primary household-level data. Unit of analysis is utility/agency actors and national policy reports, not households. Part of a Grigg author cluster including two more directly on-topic unscreened case studies: RD67517CB43CE (Jackson/Flint water failures, IAD framework) and R16A3197AFC75 (Flint drinking water failure institutional analysis) -- likely warrant retrieval.

title: Influence of National Government and Development Partners on Uganda's Water, Sanitation, and Solid Waste Services Delivery: A Review
authors: Sakaya R.; Niwagaba C.; Katukiza A.; Lüthi C.
exclusion_reason_detail: Mixed-methods review: 10 KIIs with sector experts (MWE, private sector, NGOs, development partners) triangulated with systematic literature review (65 documents). Unit of analysis is national sector/institution throughout, using aggregate performance indicators; no household-level survey/interview data. Enforcement/decentralization findings exist but at institutional scale. Same pattern as Gallegos IWRM review (R2D6E5154CE63). Borderline -- flagged for second-reviewer attention. Sibling paper R7170047A72DF (political economy barriers, Ugandan towns) not yet screened.

title: Water security and the hydro-social cycle in Catalonia: Diagnosis and challenges for a country under pressure
authors: Romero-Gomez G.
exclusion_reason_detail: Non-systematic narrative diagnostic essay (author's doctoral thesis chapter; no defined search strategy) surveying Catalonia's water security across four dimensions. No new primary empirical data -- cites the author's own already-published studies (Romero-Gómez et al. 2024a, 2024b) rather than reporting new findings. Same pattern as Elmi and Ibrahim (RF7BD856CF4EE) and Choumert-Nkolo and Phélinas (R989941A73A26). Flags sibling paper RC78DCEC4F3E0 (Sauri, Yoon and Romero-Gómez, 'Lived experiences of water poverty in Barcelona', 2026) as likely primary fieldwork worth retrieving.

title: Effectiveness of measures taken by governments to support hand hygiene in community settings: a systematic review
authors: Snyder J.S. et al.
exclusion_reason_detail: Formal PRISMA systematic review (12 databases, 31 studies, 19 countries) of government measures supporting hand hygiene practices, categorized via the Sanitation and Water for All Building Blocks framework. Outcome is hand hygiene behavior/practice, not water/sanitation service access -- outside this review outcome hierarchy. Flags a Snyder/Freeman cluster: R1811F8F093C3 (PAASIM urban water supply, Mozambique) and RE4B8992DC140 (private sector sanitation, Nairobi informal settlement schools), both unscreened and more directly on-topic.

title: Enhancing the educational environment for optimal menstrual hygiene management in Kisangani, Democratic Republic of Congo
authors: Ngandru Kiza A. et al.
exclusion_reason_detail: Structured observational assessment of WASH infrastructure in 38 secondary schools in Kisangani, DRC, for menstrual hygiene management. Population is schools/adolescent girl students, not households. No legal/administrative household-level access mechanism examined. Same wrong-population pattern as Zaman (R762C6673156D), Sinharoy ARISE (R8AC9D969EC05), and Adekunle (R2ABF219B5CB4).

title: Priorities for the rural water and sanitation services regulation in Latin America
authors: Alvarez L.; Vargas L.; Jimenez A.
exclusion_reason_detail: Desk review plus expert-consultation process (80+ experts, 14 regulators/institutions, LAC) producing 11 regulatory policy priorities for rural WASH services. Not a systematic review (no defined search strategy); no primary household-level empirical data or outcome evaluation -- a policy-recommendation report. Contains substantive country-specific regulatory examples that may be worth citing as background. Borderline -- flagged for second-reviewer attention.

title: INTEGRATED WATER RESOURCE MANAGEMENT IN ACHIEVING SDG 6: A COMPARATIVE STUDY
authors: Iraguha L.; Ofuyatan O.; Olukanni D.O.
exclusion_reason_detail: Conference proceedings comparative desk review (Nigeria vs. Rwanda) of IWRM progress toward SDG 6, using secondary national SDG Indicator 6.5.1 survey data, not household-level data. Unit of analysis is the country, not the household. Same pattern as Gallegos IWRM review (R2D6E5154CE63).
